has a long legacy. We organize and resist in context-specific ways.

Right now we are experiencing a backlash. But #metoo is one iteration of a long legacy.

Saying #RIPmetoo is an act of erasure. It obscures those of us who continue to fight.

Who does it serve?  2/

I keep seeing posts about #metoo is dead or #RIPmetoo. It's not dead and it's not over. Here's why:

Feminist movements—and all movements to end oppression—are iterative and dynamic. They respond to their times. We respond to our times.

to carry on with the work.

But women have been fighting back for a long time. And now is a time to rally, to connect, to build solidarity and mutual aid with women and trans and nonbinary folx.

#metoo will be relevant as long as there is a need to say, "it happened to me, too."
